featured_reviews.name: Le écrivaine
featured_reviews.review_text:
The first worship centre in Mumbai of the Kerala-based Malankara Orthodox Syrian Church – also known as the Indian Orthodox Church. The original church was consecrated on 9th December 1951. This first church of the Malankara Orthodox Christians of Mumbai, which
celebrated the diamond jubilee in the year 2009, was elevated to the rank of Cathedral in the same year, by an His Holiness Moran Mar Baselius Marthoma Didymos I, seventh Catholicos of the East.
Like the other Kerala-based Malankara Mar Thoma Syrian Church, this is another church of the ethnic Saint Thomas Christian community, which had its origin in the evangelical activity of Thomas – an Apostle of Jesus Christ, in the 1st century. (Malankara is an historical name of modern Kerala).
All the ‘Syrian’ churches in the early days, had their liturgy in Syriac – an ancient Middle Eastern language, and acknowledged the spiritual leadership of the Syriac Orthodox Patriarch of Antioch. To make it more relevant to worshippers, both churches now have their liturgy in Malayalam. (Antioch, then a city of ancient Syria, is now in south-central Turkey, near the Syrian border. This location is believed to have been the cradle of early Jewish-Gentile Christianity.)
On account of the limited space available on the plot leased from the Bombay Municipal Corporation, the cathedral itself is of modest proportions. No parking is available in the premises, or even on the roads outside. A night school is conducted in the basement.
The cathedral is not very far from Dadar station – where the Western and Central railway lines converge. So it is convenient for commuters from both the Western and Eastern suburban areas of the city. Those coming the Navi Mumbai area (by Harbour line) would have to shift at Kurla to a train on the Central Railway line.
This church is near an old landmark – the Dadar T.T. (tram terminus), which has now become obscure. There are plenty of buses – both BEST and state transport, running close by.
Another Dadar landmark is what is known today as the Portuguese Church. A Catholic church (Ossa Senhora de Salvação) was originally built at this location by the Portuguese Franciscans in 1596. But, this is quite a distance from the St. Mary's Orthodox Cathedral.
During the cotton mill era of Mumbai, Dadar was the location of the largest mills – Bombay Dyeing (Spring Mills), Gold Mohur Mills, Kohinoor Mills, Ruby Mills and Tata Mills, were in the neighbourhood.
[☞ I am a member of another Christian denomination, i.e., I'm not a member of the Malankara Mar Thoma Syrian Church.
This review is meant to ‘enlighten’ those who aren't members of this church, incl. non-Christians.]

featured_reviews.name: Madhavan
featured_reviews.review_text:
This church isn’t just another place of worship — it’s one of the oldest in Mumbai, with origins that trace back over 400 years to the Portuguese Franciscan era. The original structure has been rebuilt multiple times, and the current building — completed in the 1970s — was redesigned by renowned architect Charles Correa, giving it a distinctive, almost modernist architectural character that sets it apart from traditional church designs. There’s even a special skylight in the baptistery designed by celebrated artist M.F. Husain, adding an artistic touch to the sacred space.

Visitors and worshippers consistently describe the church as a peaceful and reflective haven, providing a calming contrast to the busy streets outside. Many find the quiet interiors, gentle lighting, and sense of reverence deeply moving — whether they’ve come to pray or simply to sit in contemplation.

Inside during Mass, there’s often a beautiful choir and uplifting biblical artwork, which many visitors highlight as especially moving. The church’s atmosphere is welcoming to both regular parishioners and first-time visitors.

Conveniently located just a short walk from Dadar station, it’s easy to visit whether you’re a local or a traveller exploring the city’s heritage sites. The church also serves as a well-known landmark in the neighbourhood, sitting comfortably among the vibrant life of Dadar West.

Our Lady of Salvation Church is much more than a place of worship — it’s a living piece of Mumbai’s cultural and architectural history. Whether you’re drawn by its spiritual significance, curious about its design, or simply seeking a quiet moment amidst city life, it’s a highly recommended stop in Dadar.

featured_reviews.name: Sun Jay
featured_reviews.review_text:
Our Lady of Salvation Church, also known as the Portuguese Church, is a truly unique and beautiful place of worship in Dadar West. The church is exceptionally well maintained and always kept clean, providing a peaceful and serene environment for prayer and reflection.

Its modern architectural design makes it stand out among Mumbai’s churches — both striking and spiritual at the same time. Located just about a 10-minute walk from Dadar Railway Station (West), it’s easily accessible and a must-visit for anyone in the area.

Whether you’re attending Mass or simply stopping by for a quiet moment, this church offers a sense of calm amidst the busy city life. A wonderful landmark of faith and heritage in the heart of Mumbai.

featured_reviews.review_text:
A very silent and peaceful Shrine. The Shrine of Don Bosco's Madonna, also known as Don Bosco Church Matunga, is a famous church in Mumbai and a popular spot for Marian devotees. Construction work started with imported marble from Italy in 1954 and completed in 1957. The exterior of the church is clad with Indian granite. It contains a lot of stained glass art work also.

The Shrine is located in Matunga East, adjacent to Don Bosco School and the compound also has football, hockey, cricket, volleyball and basketball training facilities as part of the educational institutions located in the same campus.

The church is a must-visit spot for Marian devotees and is considered part of Mumbai’s heritage.

Shrine Office Timings are Monday to Friday 9:00 am to 12 noon and 2 pm to 5:30 pm, Saturday 7:00 am to 12 noon and 2pm to 6:45 pm, and Sunday 7:00 am to 12 noon. There are many masses from 6am from Sunday and evening at 6pm..

description:
The Church of Our Lady of Dolours, Wadala is a Roman Catholic church in Mumbai, India built in 1853. The parish of Our Lady of Dolours with its school, St. Joseph's was entrusted to the Salesians in 1948, about the same time as the Salesians settled in Matunga. The school was co-ed until the Salesian Sisters came into the Wadala Village with the Auxilium Convent for girls. The centerpiece of the church is a statue of the Pieta.

The parish extends till Kings Circle fly-over in the North, Naigaum, Sahakar Nagar and Kidwai Nagar in the South, Hindu Colony/Ruia College in the West and the Harbour Branch Railway line including the Reynold's Road, BPT Quarters in the East.

featured_reviews.name: Joseph Nunes
featured_reviews.review_text:
St. Andrew’s Church, with its 400+ years of rich history, has recently undergone a transformative 20-month renovation that beautifully preserves its heritage while rejuvenating its spiritual ambiance.

✨ Architectural Revival
Façade and Roof Rejuvenation: Heritage specialists like Jivraj Sankhat and Savani Heritage Conservation expertly restored the church’s iconic roof, façade, marble, woodwork, and stained-glass windows, reviving their original splendor.

Traditional Techniques: The renovation prioritized authenticity. Over 5.5 ft thick walls were replastered with lime instead of cement—an effort to maintain the church’s historical integrity.

🌞 Rediscovered Beauty
Choir Loft & Lighting: Long-hidden architectural gems, such as the choir loft’s clerestory windows, were uncovered—reintroducing natural light into the nave and restoring a key visual element of the original design.

💒 Interior Elegance
Faithfully Restored Altars: The Portuguese-inspired altars, once scarred by moisture and termite damage, were carefully conserved and revived to their former glory.

Wooden Pulpit Revival: Carved with biblical narrative, the original pulpit was meticulously restored, complete with its ornate canopy—allowing worshippers to once more feel its spiritual resonance.

⏳ Heritage Sensitivity & Community Effort
Meticulous, Not Hasty: From April 2024 to December 2025, the renovation focused on preservation over superficial repairs—respecting the church’s Portuguese colonial architecture.

Community-Driven, Funded by Love: Entirely financed by parishioners and diaspora support, the project faced financial hurdles—yet the community’s unwavering commitment ensured the work reached its homestretch.

🎖 A Joyous Reopening
On a beautiful Sunday evening, over a thousand worshippers celebrated the church’s rededication—blessed by Cardinal Oswald Gracias—marking a poignant return to its rightful spiritual grandeur.

In summary, the recent renovations at St. Andrew’s Church masterfully balance respect for its centuries-old heritage with modern integrity. From the reimagined façade to the restored interior treasures, every detail reflects love, care, and unwavering faith. It’s a testament to what can be achieved when a community unites to preserve its legacy—and a spiritually uplifting sanctuary reborn.

featured_reviews.name: Partha S Mondal
featured_reviews.review_text:
The Basilica of Our Lady of the Mount popularly known as Mount Mary Church is a historic Roman Catholic shrine in Bandra, Mumbai, perched on a foot hill overlooking the Arabian Sea. Known for its neo-Gothic architecture and 16th-century statue of the Virgin Mary, it is a major pilgrimage center drawing people of all faiths.

Many visitors come to Mount St Mary Church in order to make their mannat wish come true.

Place is very well maintained.

featured_reviews.name: Gaurav
featured_reviews.review_text: The Basilica of Our Lady of the Mount (Mount Mary Church) in Bandra is a beautiful and peaceful place with great spiritual significance. The architecture is stunning, and the atmosphere is calm and soothing. Located near Bandstand, it also offers lovely views of the sea. The church is very well maintained and attracts people of all faiths. During the annual Mount Mary Fair, the place becomes vibrant and lively. A must-visit landmark in Mumbai for peace, faith, and history.

featured_reviews.name: Anugraha Ghale
featured_reviews.review_text:
We arrived around 6 PM just as Mass was happening, and the church was beautifully filled with people, a mix of locals and visitors. Even though we didn’t stay for the full service or take part in any activities, it was lovely just to sit for a moment and take in the serenity. The architecture is stunning, especially as the evening light hits the façade.

Bandra itself is such an interesting part of Mumbai a blend of old Portuguese roots, coastal charm, and modern city rhythm. The basilica, built during the 16th century by the Portuguese, still carries traces of that heritage in its architecture and stone walls. You can almost feel how it’s stood as an anchor through centuries of storms, festivals, and city life. Don’t miss 10 min walk to the fort!

featured_reviews.name: Sushil kumar kushwaha
featured_reviews.review_text:
Basilica of Our Lady of the Mount Church situated atop Mount Mary, Bandra West is one of the most revered churches in Mumbai.
Mary Church is the statue of Our Lady of the Mount, also known as the Mother Mary. It is a spiritual sanctuary built in semi Gothic style.
The architecture combines grandeur with serenity and offers a visually rich and spiritually enriching experience for visitors.
An older structure housing the original statue of Mary, and nearby is the Our Lady of Fatima Oratory, built in 1954, featuring a marble statue of Our Lady of Fatima and the message of Fatima.
Prayer times typically run from early morning (around 5:30 AM) to evening (7:30 PM) on weekdays and Sundays,
The Church attracts devotees from all faiths for its belief in miracles, with many lighting candles in thanksgiving for favors granted !!!

featured_reviews.name: Shakeel Ahmed
featured_reviews.review_text:
The Basilica of Our Lady of the Mount, colloquially known as Mount Bandra and Mount St Mary Church; is a basilica (shrine) of the Roman Catholic Church, located at the Bandra neighbourhood of Bombay (Mumbai), India.

The story of Mount Mary Church in Bandra begins in the 1570s when Jesuit priests built a small mud-and-stone oratory on a hill overlooking the Arabian Sea in Bandra. They brought a statue of Our Lady to this location, and this event marked the beginning of the shrine's history.

The original statue is believed to have been miraculously recovered after being thrown into the sea, and a more permanent basilica was later built on the site, which has become a place of pilgrimage and peace for people of all faiths, particularly Hindus and Christians. The current church, a semi-Gothic structure, was rebuilt in 1904 and is now known as the Basilica of Our Lady of the Mount.

featured_reviews.name: Cedric Noronha
featured_reviews.review_text: A historic Roman Catholic Church located in Jacob Circle. Built in 1913, this church is dedicated to St. Ignatius Loyola. It is one of the oldest churches in Mumbai. Its interior is beautiful having wooden pews, stained glass window panes, supporting pillars etc. There is a wall carving of the Last Supper above the Altar. The facade of this church had a statue of Jesus Christ above it. There is a belfry tower at the side of the church. Also, there is a Latin inscription at the entrance. It has a school attached to it. Had attended a funeral mass service in this church in English language. It is an ideal place for local devotees as well as people of other faith.

featured_reviews.name: Terence Correia
featured_reviews.review_text:
St. Ignatius Church is where my faith, friendships, and fondest memories were all nurtured. It was here that I was baptized, received my First Communion, and was confirmed, milestones that marked the beginning of my spiritual journey. As a child and youth, I was an active part of the Legion of Mary and St. Anthony’s group, served as an altar server, and joined the youth and prayer groups. I loved helping with church cleaning, decorating the crib, making the Christmas star, and organizing events, all while laughing and playing around the church compound with friends who became like family.

Those days were filled with joy, service, and deep connections, memories I treasure even now. Seeing the church restored to its former glory, after more than 100 years since its foundation, fills my heart with happiness. St. Ignatius Church remains a timeless place of faith, community, and love, where every stone tells the story of generations who have grown, served, and celebrated here.

featured_reviews.name: The Lone Crusader
featured_reviews.review_text:
A very familiar sight often greets passersby at the North-West corner of the iconic Shivaji Park in Amchi Mumbai. Most of the nearby residents and local old-timers who routinely visit the Park, while indulging in brisk walking exercises or simply enjoying a leisurely stroll, slow down at the turn just next to the Scout Hall to pay homage to and seek blessings at a very lovely Cross nestled in the corner. The Cross, which is now part of the Holy Cross Chapel, dates back to a time way before the Park itself was created and inaugurated publicly in 1925. The origins of the Cross are steeped in history, being erected 110 years ago, according to the very affable local caretaker, Mr. Joseph Fernandes. Joseph Uncle, as he is popularly called, religiously takes care of the Chapel daily, ensuring that fresh flowers and garlands are offered to the Lord. In his words, "The Cross has always been a source of solace and blessings for all, and is reputed to fulfill one's wishes on offering heartfelt prayers. Before 1978, an old Cross (made of cement and stone, see old black & white file pictures) was standing at the very same place but unfortunately the shoulders of the Cross were damaged, tilting it at a slight angle. Instead of discarding it, the old Cross was concealed within the new Cross, which is made of marble." Collage photos comparing the two show the Scout Hall in the background, with the old iron water tanks belonging to the Scout Hall, being replaced by Sintex plastic tanks. Also see the earlier grass and shrubs where the Cross stood, now replaced by attractive floor tiles.

The Cross is given a fresh coat of paint every year or so. A shed has been erected about 20 years to protect the chapel from bird litter and other falling debris, along with an attractive candle house in metal, which is placed on a rounded pedestal made of black granite stone. The surrounding area too has been cleared of shrubs and grass, and the flooring has been fitted with marble tiles. The present Cross is an imposing but comforting structure, made from white marble and supported by an identically white prism-shaped pedestal. The front of the Cross depicts Lord Jesus on the crucifix, with INRI (which is the Latin abbreviation of 'Jesus of Nazareth, King of the Jews') being inscribed in brass at the top.

The Chapel is now part of the recently registered Shivaji Park Ground Trust. A Rosary is held on 2nd October of every year as an annual ritual, and attended by dignitaries of the nearby Portuguese, Victoria and St. Michael Churches.

The Cross will always be a source of solace for those who seek it, continuing to instill good values in and shower blessings on all who pass by with devotion within their hearts!!!!
